title: zForth on CP/M-80 (Z80) — the DOS-native Forth, on a non-DOS target

components.source: src/zforth/zforth.c + forth/core.zf (zevv/zForth) + cpmmain.c + crt0.s, built with SDCC (z80)

toolchain.target: cpm80 (Z80 CP/M 2.2 .COM, 32-bit integer cell, BDOS console + file read)

notes: The SAME tiny Forth the lab ships as a DOS program (projects/forth-dos), recompiled for a NON-DOS target, and — like forth-dos — it READS ITS PROGRAM from a mounted PROG.FTH (over CP/M BDOS open/read-sequential), so it runs ARBITRARY Code-tab Forth output, not a fixed demo. zForth's DOS build uses float cells and printf/sscanf/fopen, none SDCC-z80 friendly; this build uses a 32-bit INTEGER cell (division is integer: 7/2 == 3 — the one deliberate semantic gap versus the float-cell DOS build), sends output through BDOS function 2 (cpmmain.c, no printf), reads PROG.FTH over BDOS (no C library file I/O), and compiles with ZF_ENABLE_TRACE 0 (no va_list). samples/demo.fth is an arbitrary Code-tab-shaped program (a `: banner ;` word, `7 7 *`, a counted `( repeat )` begin/until loop, a running total); proof.mjs boots FORTH.COM on the bw-board z80 machine via runMediaBundle with a minimal BDOS console+file shim, mounts demo.fth as PROG.FTH, and checks the transcript. In brickwright-lite the full lite BDOS layer (cpm-z80.js) serves the same file reads, so runCpmProgram runs arbitrary generated Forth on the Z80/CP-M bench. build.sh rebuilds FORTH.COM byte-for-byte. crt0.s is BrickWright's CP/M crt0 (BSD-2-Clause, shared with projects/cpm-software); zForth is MIT.
